findings.title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts
findings.body: When a slot overlaps a date override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking busy times. This affects both fixed and round-robin hosts, including personal events. For example, an override allowing 10:00–11:00 makes a 10:00 slot available even when an accepted booking or external calendar event occupies that time. An override should replace working hours, not bypass conflict checks.

findings.title: Require the entire booking to fit within an override
findings.body: The override checks reject only disjoint intervals, so any partial overlap is treated as availability. With a fixed-host override of 10:00–11:00, a 60-minute slot generated for another host at 09:30 or 10:30 passes, despite extending outside the fixed host's availability. A slot starting exactly at 11:00 also passes because isAfter excludes equality. Both booking boundaries must be contained in an allowed override interval.

findings.title: Split working hours cause every slot to be rejected
findings.body: The new working-hours guard rejects a slot if it is outside any interval on that weekday, rather than accepting it if it is inside an interval. For a normal schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00 UTC, morning slots fail against the afternoon interval and afternoon slots fail against the morning interval. Consequently, personal and team events using lunch-break schedules become unbookable even without date overrides.

findings.title: The working-hours end check uses the slot's start time
findings.body: Both start and end are calculated from slotStartTime, so the check never verifies that the booking finishes within the host's working hours. For example, a fixed host available 09:00–10:00 passes validation for a 60-minute slot at 09:30 generated by another round-robin host's date override. This permits bookings extending beyond the fixed host's availability; end must be calculated from slotEndTime.

findings.title: Apply overrides according to the host's local calendar date
findings.body: The override's converted start and the slot are compared by UTC calendar date, but a date override replaces a day in the host's timezone. For a Kolkata fixed host normally available Monday 00:00–01:00, a Monday override of 14:00–15:00 must remove the regular early-morning availability. A slot on Sunday at 19:00 UTC is Monday 00:30 locally, yet this comparison misses the override and allows it through the regular working-hours check. Overrides can also incorrectly suppress availability on the adjacent local day.

findings.title: Multiple override intervals reject each other's slots
findings.body: dateOverrides.find searches for any same-day interval that does not overlap the slot. If a host has two override windows, such as 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00, a slot in the first window is rejected by the second, and a slot in the second is rejected by the first. Valid split date overrides therefore produce no availability. The check must accept a slot contained in at least one window, rather than reject it for being outside another window.

findings.title: Split converted overrides when they cross attendee midnight
findings.body: The timezone conversion extracts only hours and minutes, discarding any date rollover. A 20:00–23:00 UTC override viewed in UTC+2 becomes startTime 1320 (22:00) and endTime 60 (01:00). buildSlots treats this as an invalid interval because startTime exceeds endTime, so a personal event loses the entire override instead of showing its portions on the two attendee dates. Preserve the converted dates and split the interval at midnight.

findings.title: Override timezone conversion applies DST correction twice
findings.body: The new offset uses timezone offsets on the override date, so the resulting minutes already account for that date's DST. buildSlots subsequently adds organizerDSTDiff minus inviteeDSTDiff, which is intended to correct working hours calculated with today's offsets. For example, while New York is on UTC−4, a future January override of 10:00–11:00 New York converts correctly to 15:00–16:00 UTC here, but buildSlots shifts it again to 16:00–17:00. Override slots need to avoid that additional correction.
